RECOMMENDATION: IT DEPENDS
LIKELIHOOD: 40

An all-male panel is not evidence of discrimination by itself — it's common in economics and often reflects the department's existing composition. It is relevant as context, not as your main argument.

Your stronger facts are concrete: completed vs. unfinished PhD, six papers vs. two, four years of teaching — against a criterion ("industry experience") that may not have been weighted in the advertised requirements. Check the job posting. If industry experience wasn't listed or was marginal, that's a defensible complaint.

First, escalate the unanswered request in writing, citing any statutory deadline for written reasons at a public institution. Mention panel composition only as supporting context, and ask how the criteria were scored.
